correctness.rationale: Every negative root has an explicit complementary-coordinate positive-root convex witness with norm squared 12/[(n-3)(n-2)(n-1)] for n≥5. The farthest negative highest root satisfies all projection KKT inequalities, while a strictly improving root direction excludes every competitor. Rational low-dimensional certificates cover n=2,3,4. Convexity proves uniqueness over the entire full root polytope. Exact standard-library checks (n=2..16, plus n=30,61,103 projection checks) and 220 independent numerical QPs (n=2..11) were executed from the included paths; finite checks support but do not replace proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The nearest prior sphere center implies our supporting minimum-norm lemma after noting its root scalar products; we credit it explicitly and exclude that lemma as a stand-alone novelty. From that premise one still must prove the global complementary-coordinate bound, the highest negative-root KKT inequalities, the strict competitors, and the two exceptional small-dimensional computations. The previous claims are not equivalent to, nor broader than, these joint assertions.

value.rationale: The standard complete transitive-orientation polytope and its bidirected root hull are canonical geometric objects. Exact Hausdorff separation, unique extremal root and full nonvertex projection solve a motivated whole-polytope comparison, while the n=4-to-5 change in the projection support and cubic asymptotic excess are structural features not captured by known face counts or enclosing spheres.
